mkey-01-c1.text: Reginald Scot (ed. Brinsley Nicholson) (1584). The Discoverie of Witchcraft. Project Gutenberg (1886 reprint of the 1584 first edition).
mkey-01-c1.quote: But in shewing feats, and juggling with cards, the principall point consisteth in shuffling them nimblie, and alwaies keeping one certeine card either in the bottome, or in some knowne place of the stocke
mkey-01-c1.claim: the principal point of juggling with cards was always keeping one certain card either in the bottom, or in some known place of the stock

mkey-01-c3.text: Reginald Scot (ed. Brinsley Nicholson) (1584). The Discoverie of Witchcraft. Project Gutenberg (1886 reprint of the 1584 first edition).
mkey-01-c3.quote: Hereby you shall seeme to worke woonders; for it will be easie for you to see or spie one card, which though you be perceived to doo, it will not be suspected, if you shuffle them well afterwards.
mkey-01-c3.claim: it will be easy for you to see or spy one card

mkey-02-c1.text: Reginald Scot (ed. Brinsley Nicholson) (1584). The Discoverie of Witchcraft. Project Gutenberg (1886 reprint of the 1584 first edition).
mkey-02-c1.quote: when you feele it, you may there hold it, untill you have shuffled over the cards againe, still leaving your kept card below
mkey-02-c1.claim: when you feel it you hold it there until you have shuffled over the cards again, still leaving the kept card below

mkey-02-c1.text: Reginald Scot (ed. Brinsley Nicholson) (1584). The Discoverie of Witchcraft. Project Gutenberg (1886 reprint of the 1584 first edition).
mkey-02-c1.quote: Being perfect herein, you may doo almost what you list with the cards.
mkey-02-c1.claim: you may do almost what you list with the cards

mkey-02-c1.text: Reginald Scot (ed. Brinsley Nicholson) (1584). The Discoverie of Witchcraft. Project Gutenberg (1886 reprint of the 1584 first edition).
mkey-02-c1.quote: though it consist of eight, twelve, or twentie cards, you may keepe them still together unsevered next to the nether card, and yet shuffle them often to satisfie the curious beholders
mkey-02-c1.claim: a packet of eight, twelve or twenty cards can be kept together next to the bottom card while you still shuffle them often to satisfy the curious beholders

mkey-03-c1.text: Gustav Kuhn, Hugo A. Caffaratti, Rob Teszka, Ronald A. Rensink (2014). A psychologically-based taxonomy of misdirection. Frontiers in Psychology.
mkey-03-c1.quote: The use of such delays is therefore an important kind of memory misdirection, and one of the reasons why magicians typically attempt to separate in time the method from the effect
mkey-03-c1.claim: People remember more of an event immediately after it has occurred, as compared to some time later

mkey-03-c1.text: Gustav Kuhn, Hugo A. Caffaratti, Rob Teszka, Ronald A. Rensink (2014). A psychologically-based taxonomy of misdirection. Frontiers in Psychology.
mkey-03-c1.quote: attentional de-emphasis can occur once a magic trick has been concluded: if the magician picks up a bowl in preparation for his next trick, say, the audience won't suspect the execution of the method at that time.
mkey-03-c1.claim: attentional de-emphasis can occur once a magic trick has been concluded

mkey-03-c3.text: Gustav Kuhn, Hugo A. Caffaratti, Rob Teszka, Ronald A. Rensink (2014). A psychologically-based taxonomy of misdirection. Frontiers in Psychology.
mkey-03-c3.quote: Our psychologically-based taxonomy has three basic categories, corresponding to the types of psychological mechanisms affected: perception, memory, and reasoning.
mkey-03-c3.claim: The psychologists divide misdirection into three kinds of mechanism: perception, memory and reasoning.

mkey-03-c3.text: Gustav Kuhn, Hugo A. Caffaratti, Rob Teszka, Ronald A. Rensink (2014). A psychologically-based taxonomy of misdirection. Frontiers in Psychology.
mkey-03-c3.quote: “magic is misdirection and misdirection is magic” (Hugard, 1960 , p. 115)
mkey-03-c3.claim: One writer on magic, Hugard, put it as "magic is misdirection and misdirection is magic"

mkey-04-c1.text: Reginald Scot (ed. Brinsley Nicholson) (1584). The Discoverie of Witchcraft. Project Gutenberg (1886 reprint of the 1584 first edition).
mkey-04-c1.quote: WHen you have seene a card privilie, or as though you marked it not, laie the same undermost, and shuffle the cards as before you are taught, till your card lie againe below in the bottome.
mkey-04-c1.claim: In his version, the performer sees a card privately, lays it undermost, and shuffles until it lies at the bottom again.

mkey-04-c1.text: Reginald Scot (ed. Brinsley Nicholson) (1584). The Discoverie of Witchcraft. Project Gutenberg (1886 reprint of the 1584 first edition).
mkey-04-c1.quote: Then shew the same to the beholders, willing them to remember it: then shuffle the cards, or let anie other shuffle them; for you know the card alreadie, and therefore may at anie time tell them what card they saw
mkey-04-c1.claim: Then he shows it to the beholders so that they remember it, lets anyone shuffle the cards, and tells them what card they saw, since he knew it all along.

mkey-04-c3.text: Reginald Scot (ed. Brinsley Nicholson) (1584). The Discoverie of Witchcraft. Project Gutenberg (1886 reprint of the 1584 first edition).
mkey-04-c3.quote: but thinke one of them three, and by his eie you shall assuredlie perceive which he both seeth and thinketh.
mkey-04-c3.claim: by his eie you shall assuredlie perceive which he both seeth and thinketh

mkey-05-c1.text: Reginald Scot (ed. Brinsley Nicholson) (1584). The Discoverie of Witchcraft. Project Gutenberg (1886 reprint of the 1584 first edition).
mkey-05-c1.quote: Wherein the lewde dealing of witches and witchmongers is notablie detected, the knauerie of coniurors
mkey-05-c1.claim: "the lewde dealing of witches and witchmongers is notablie detected, the knauerie of coniurors"

mkey-05-c3.text: Reginald Scot (ed. Brinsley Nicholson) (1584). The Discoverie of Witchcraft. Project Gutenberg (1886 reprint of the 1584 first edition).
mkey-05-c3.quote: Of cards, with good cautions how to avoid cousenage therein: speciall rules to conveie and handle the cards
mkey-05-c3.claim: Of cards, with good cautions how to avoid cousenage therein

mkey-05-c3.text: Reginald Scot (ed. Brinsley Nicholson) (1584). The Discoverie of Witchcraft. Project Gutenberg (1886 reprint of the 1584 first edition).
mkey-05-c3.quote: I dare not (as I could) shew the lewd juggling that chetors practise, least it minister some offense to the well disposed, to the simple hurt and losses, and to the wicked occasion of evill dooing.
mkey-05-c3.claim: he dared not (as he could) show the lewd juggling that cheaters practise
